bindings.fact: HEADING config degrees multiplied by float00b42f0c, stored at config+0x20.
Orbit uses heading at camera+0x20: source eyeXY=focusXY-horizontal*[cos(H),sin(H)]. Existing pitch/distance/terrain/fov branches retained.
Increment yaw negates its input in orbit mode1, then wraps into[0,float2PI).
Absolute yaw setter wraps into[0,float2PI) without negation.
Builds 3x3 source rotation from pitch and(H-PI/2). Columns are native forward/up/right.
World-to-camera subtracts cached eye, applies inverse of the native3x3, then reorders localD/U/R intoR/U/D.
Camera basis is copied to NiCamera rotation+0x38; unchanged horizontal frustum is +/-tan(FOV/2),vertical divided by aspect.

adapter.heading: cam.heading is radians relative to native configured90 degrees, normalized[-PI,PI); missing/nonfinite0.
adapter.positive: Camera orbit moves from south toward east; +PI/2 puts eye east of focus and looks west.
adapter.coordinateMapping: SourceXYZ -> browserX/Z/-Y. The previous north-up orientation is calibrated to exactly0 to preserve its numeric output.
adapter.groundForward: [-sin(heading),-cos(heading)] in simulationX/Y; screen-down is its negative.
adapter.ray: direction=forward+right*ndcX*tanX+up*ndcY*tanY. Not normalized: its parameter is forward camera depth, exactly the near/far clip convention.
adapter.terrain: Height sampling uses rotated eyeXY; native minimum clearance/pitch correction preserved.

api.updateOriginalCamera: (cam,view,width,height,heightAt,profile) reads/normalizescam.heading and fills the existing view contract plus rotated basis.
api.originalCameraRay: (view,px,py,width,height) returns the unnormalized rotated world direction.

mathAndBaseline.scope: North baseline bit equality, independent native00520600 basis, heading orbit/pan, rotated terrain clearance, camera-depth ray endpoints and projection. UI input rate remains an adapter.

nativeGles.scope: Native GLES point draw/readback consumes production camera matrices and points from public picking rays. Tests 0/45/90/180 degrees, four zooms, expected screen pixels, and near/far/behind-eye clipping. No original runtime or UI launched.

limits: Native CamCtrl token-to-delta, repeat timing and Shift speed multiplier have not been proved; input rate remains a frontend adapter.
The relative-radian API uses JavaScript trigonometry and a calibrated north basis; full x87 instruction-level equality for arbitrary rotations is not claimed.
